PADHIQ · CLASS 9 SCIENCE · CHAPTER 01
Matter in Our Surroundings
States · Changes · Evaporation · Latent Heat
✦ ONE-PAGER HITZZ ✦
"ज्ञान is the heat that transforms the solid mind into a flowing stream of understanding."
⚡ Key Formulas Latent Heat Fusion = 3.36×10⁵ J/kgLatent Heat Vaporisation = 2.26×10⁶ J/kgEcho min dist = 17.2 m
◆ Quick Revision Points ◆
Three States of Matter
  • Solid: particles closest, strongest IMF
  • Liquid: medium spacing, flows
  • Gas: farthest, weakest force
  • Compressibility: Gas ≫ Liquid ≫ Solid
Evaporation Increases When
  • Temperature increases
  • Surface area increases
  • Wind speed increases
  • Humidity decreases → causes cooling effect
Sublimation Examples
  • Camphor ⭐(most important)
  • Dry ice (solid CO₂, −78.5°C)
  • Naphthalene (mothballs)
  • Ammonium chloride
  • Iodine
Key Facts to Remember
  • Steam burns more than boiling water (extra latent heat)
  • Pressure cooker: ↑P → ↑bp
  • Mountains: ↓P → ↓bp
  • Evaporation ≠ Boiling

PADHIQ · CLASS 9 SCIENCE · CHAPTER 02
Is Matter Around Us Pure?
Pure Substances · Mixtures · Colloids · Separation Methods
✦ ONE-PAGER HITZZ ✦
"Like purifying gold from ore, the wise student separates knowledge from mere information."
⚡ Key Formulas Tyndall Effect = 1–100 nm particlesSolution < 1 nm · Suspension > 100 nm
◆ Quick Revision Points ◆
Types of Mixtures
  • Solution: <1 nm, no Tyndall, transparent
  • Colloid: 1–100 nm, Tyndall ✓
  • Suspension: >100 nm, settles on standing
Separation Methods
  • Evaporation → solid from solution
  • Distillation → liquids by bp
  • Chromatography → dyes
  • Centrifugation → cream from milk
Pure vs Mixture
  • Pure: fixed composition, definite mp/bp
  • Mixture: variable composition
  • Alloy = homogeneous metal mixture
  • Amalgam = alloy of Hg
Key Examples (Exam!)
  • Air = homogeneous mixture
  • Sea water = mixture
  • Brass = Cu+Zn
  • Blood = colloid
  • NaCl solution = true solution

PADHIQ · CLASS 9 SCIENCE · CHAPTER 03
Atoms and Molecules
Laws of Chemical Combination · Atomic Mass · Mole Concept
✦ ONE-PAGER HITZZ ✦
"One mole of dedication contains 6.022×10²³ moments of practice — Avogadro of efforts!"
⚡ Key Formulas 1 mol = 6.022×10²³ particlesn = mass ÷ molar massVol at STP = n × 22.4 L
◆ Quick Revision Points ◆
Valency (Combining Power)
  • H, Cl, Na, K, F → valency 1
  • O, Mg, Ca, Zn → valency 2
  • Al → valency 3
  • Fe: 2 or 3 (variable)
  • Cu: 1 or 2
Writing Chemical Formulae
  • Cross-multiply valencies
  • H₂O: H(1)×O(2)→H₂O
  • MgO: Mg(2)×O(2)→MgO
  • AlCl₃: Al(3)×Cl(1)→AlCl₃
Polyatomic Ions
  • NH₄⁺ ammonium (1)
  • OH⁻ hydroxide (1)
  • SO₄²⁻ sulphate (2)
  • CO₃²⁻ carbonate (2)
  • NO₃⁻ nitrate (1)
Mole Calculations
  • n = mass ÷ molar mass
  • Particles = n × 6.022×10²³
  • Volume at STP = n × 22.4 L
  • % = (element mass ÷ MM) × 100

PADHIQ · CLASS 9 SCIENCE · CHAPTER 04
Structure of the Atom
Thomson · Rutherford · Bohr Model · Isotopes · Isobars
✦ ONE-PAGER HITZZ ✦
"The nucleus of wisdom is tiny yet powerful — like the guru's teaching that holds the entire universe."
⚡ Key Formulas Shell capacity = 2n²Z = protons · A = p + nIsotopes: same Z, diff A
◆ Quick Revision Points ◆
Subatomic Particles
  • Proton: +1, ~1u, in nucleus
  • Neutron: 0 charge, ~1u
  • Electron: −1, negligible mass
  • Z = protons
  • A = p+n
Bohr's Shell Model
  • Shells: K(n=1) L(n=2) M(n=3) N(n=4)
  • Max electrons: 2n²
  • Valence e⁻ = outermost
  • Octet rule: 8 = stable
Isotopes & Isobars
  • Isotopes: same Z, diff neutrons → H: ¹H ²H ³H
  • Cl-35 & Cl-37
  • Isobars: same A, diff Z → Ca-40 & Ar-40
Gold Foil Experiment
  • Most α-particles passed through
  • Few deflected
  • Very few bounced back → Nucleus: tiny, dense, positive
  • Atom = mostly empty

PADHIQ · CLASS 9 SCIENCE · CHAPTER 05
The Fundamental Unit of Life
Cell Theory · Organelles · Osmosis · Diffusion · Plant vs Animal
✦ ONE-PAGER HITZZ ✦
"Every cell is a universe unto itself — study it with the curiosity of Aryabhata studying the cosmos!"
⚡ Key Formulas Osmosis = water through semi-perm membraneDiffusion = high → low conc · No energy
◆ Quick Revision Points ◆
Cell Theory (Exam!)
  • Schleiden 1838: plants from cells
  • Schwann 1839: animals from cells
  • Virchow 1855: cells from pre-existing cells
Key Organelles
  • Nucleus: DNA (director)
  • Mitochondria: ATP (powerhouse, own DNA)
  • Ribosome: protein synthesis
  • Golgi: packaging
  • Lysosome: suicide bag
Animal vs Plant Cell
  • Cell wall: Plant✓ Animal✗
  • Chloroplast: Plant✓ Animal✗
  • Large vacuole: Plant✓
  • Centriole: Animal✓
  • Lysosome: mainly Animal
Transport Types
  • Diffusion: high→low (no energy)
  • Osmosis: water via semi-perm membrane
  • Active transport: low→high (energy needed)

PADHIQ · CLASS 9 SCIENCE · CHAPTER 06
Tissues
Plant Tissues · Animal Tissues · Structure & Function
✦ ONE-PAGER HITZZ ✦
"As tissues strengthen the body, consistent study strengthens the mind — both grow through purposeful work."
⚡ Key Formulas Xylem = water transport (unidirectional ↑)Phloem = food transport (bidirectional)
◆ Quick Revision Points ◆
Meristematic vs Permanent
  • Meristematic: actively dividing, thin wall
  • Apical=length
  • Lateral (cambium)=girth
  • Permanent: differentiated, dead possible
Xylem & Phloem
  • Xylem: mostly dead (tracheids+vessels)
  • Unidirectional roots→leaves
  • Phloem: living (sieve+companion)
  • Bidirectional
  • Together = vascular bundle
Connective Tissue Types
  • Blood: RBC, WBC, platelets, plasma
  • Bone: rigid, calcium salts
  • Cartilage: flexible, ear/nose
  • Adipose: fat/insulation
  • Areolar: fills spaces
Muscle Tissue Types
  • Striated: voluntary, limb muscles
  • Smooth: involuntary, gut/vessels
  • Cardiac: involuntary, never fatigues
  • Neuron: axon up to 1 metre long

PADHIQ · CLASS 9 SCIENCE · CHAPTER 07
Improvement in Food Resources
Crops · Manure vs Fertiliser · Irrigation · Animal Husbandry
✦ ONE-PAGER HITZZ ✦
"A farmer's wisdom and a student's dedication both yield the richest harvest when nurtured with patience."
⚡ Key Formulas Kharif: June–Sep · Rabi: Nov–Apr · Zaid: Mar–JunDrip irrigation = most water efficient
◆ Quick Revision Points ◆
Crop Improvement Methods
  • Hybridisation: cross 2 varieties
  • Introduced variety: from another region
  • GM crops: gene insertion
  • Goal: HYV — High Yielding Varieties
Irrigation Systems
  • Wells/tube wells: groundwater
  • Canal: rivers, large scale
  • Sprinkler: overhead spray
  • Drip: most efficient, direct to roots
  • Tanks: rainwater
Animal Husbandry
  • Exotic breeds: high yield (Jersey, Brown Swiss)
  • Local breeds: disease resistant
  • Crossbreeding = best of both
  • Leghorn=eggs
  • Broiler=meat
Pest & Disease Mgmt
  • Weed control: manual or weedicides
  • Pest: insects → pesticides
  • Disease: fungi/bacteria/virus
  • Biological: natural predators
  • IPM method

PADHIQ · CLASS 9 SCIENCE · CHAPTER 08
Motion
Distance · Velocity · Acceleration · Equations of Motion · Graphs
✦ ONE-PAGER HITZZ ✦
"Like Brahmaputra in motion — speed without direction is distance; with direction it becomes velocity!"
⚡ Key Formulas v = u + ats = ut + ½at²v² = u² + 2as1 km/h = 5/18 m/s
◆ Quick Revision Points ◆
Scalars vs Vectors
  • Distance: total path (scalar)
  • Displacement: shortest path + direction (vector)
  • Speed = d/t (scalar)
  • Velocity = s/t (vector)
Types of Motion
  • Uniform: equal distance in equal time
  • Non-uniform: unequal
  • Uniform acceleration: constant a
  • Retardation: negative a
  • Free fall: a=g
Graph Interpretations
  • d-t slope = speed
  • d-t straight = uniform
  • d-t curve = non-uniform
  • v-t slope = acceleration
  • v-t area = displacement
Key Values & Conversions
  • g = 9.8 m/s²
  • Speed of light = 3×10⁸ m/s
  • 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s
  • 1 m/s = 3.6 km/h
  • Equations: UNIFORM acceleration only

PADHIQ · CLASS 9 SCIENCE · CHAPTER 09
Force and Laws of Motion
Newton's 3 Laws · Inertia · Momentum · Conservation
✦ ONE-PAGER HITZZ ✦
"Newton sat under the apple tree; the wise student sits under the teacher's wisdom. Both discover universal laws!"
⚡ Key Formulas F = map = mv (momentum)F = Δp/Δt · W = mg
◆ Quick Revision Points ◆
Momentum & Impulse
  • p = mv (kg
  • m/s, vector)
  • Impulse = F×t = Δp
  • Large t → small F (catching ball safely)
  • Small t → large F (bullet impact)
Conservation of Momentum
  • m₁u₁ + m₂u₂ = m₁v₁ + m₂v₂
  • Valid: no external force
  • Recoil: gun+bullet total p=0
  • Rocket: exhaust back, rocket forward
F=ma Applications
  • Safety belt: ↑time → ↓force
  • Airbag: ↑time → ↓force
  • Bus brakes: passengers lurch forward (inertia)
  • Karate: short time → huge force
Key Formulae Summary
  • F = ma
  • p = mv
  • F = Δp/Δt
  • W = mg (weight)
  • g = 9.8 m/s²
  • Inertia ∝ mass
  • Newton (N) = kg
  • m/s²

PADHIQ · CLASS 9 SCIENCE · CHAPTER 10
Gravitation
Universal Law · g · Weight vs Mass · Buoyancy · Archimedes
✦ ONE-PAGER HITZZ ✦
"As Brahmagupta first described gravity centuries ago, let this knowledge ground your understanding firmly!"
⚡ Key Formulas F = GM₁M₂/d²g = 9.8 m/s² (Earth)g_moon = 1.67 m/s²G = 6.674×10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg²
◆ Quick Revision Points ◆
Gravitational Force
  • F ∝ M₁×M₂ (more mass → more F)
  • F ∝ 1/d² (more distance → less F)
  • G = universal constant
  • Always attractive
g vs G
  • G: universal constant (same everywhere)
  • g = 9.8 m/s² on Earth surface
  • g varies: altitude, depth, latitude
  • Weight W=mg varies; mass=constant
Thrust, Pressure, Buoyancy
  • Pressure = F/Area (Pa=N/m²)
  • Buoyant F = ρ_fluid × V × g
  • Ship floats: hollow → avg ρ < water
  • Hydrometer: measures density
Free Fall & Weight
  • Free fall: only gravity, a=g
  • v=gt
  • s=½gt²
  • v²=2gs
  • Weightlessness: no normal force
  • Weight on Moon = Weight on Earth ÷ 6

PADHIQ · CLASS 9 SCIENCE · CHAPTER 11
Work and Energy
Work · KE · PE · Conservation of Energy · Power
✦ ONE-PAGER HITZZ ✦
"Every unit of effort you invest in studies is stored as potential energy — released as success on exam day!"
⚡ Key Formulas W = F·d·cosθKE = ½mv²PE = mghP = W/t · 1 kWh = 3.6×10⁶ J
◆ Quick Revision Points ◆
When is Work = Zero?
  • F ⊥ displacement (cos90°=0)
  • No displacement (holding book)
  • Circular motion (centripetal ⊥ velocity)
  • Positive: same direction
  • Negative: opposite
Forms of Energy
  • Kinetic: ½mv² (motion)
  • Potential: mgh (height/stored)
  • Chemical: food/fuel/battery
  • Heat: molecular motion
  • Nuclear: fission/fusion
Power & Commercial Unit
  • P = W/t = F×v (Watt)
  • 1 kWh = 3.6×10⁶ Joules
  • 1 kWh = 1 unit of electricity
  • 1 Horsepower = 746 W
  • Bills are in kWh units
Energy Conservation
  • Total energy = constant
  • Pendulum: KE↔PE
  • Hydro dam: PE→KE→electrical
  • Burning: chemical→heat+light
  • No 100% efficient machine

PADHIQ · CLASS 9 SCIENCE · CHAPTER 12
Sound
Longitudinal Wave · Echo · Reverberation · SONAR · Ultrasound
✦ ONE-PAGER HITZZ ✦
"Like OM resonating through the cosmos, sound carries knowledge — be the student who truly listens deeply."
⚡ Key Formulas v = f × λEcho min dist = 17.2 mSONAR: d = v×t/2Speed in air ≈ 346 m/s
◆ Quick Revision Points ◆
Wave Properties
  • Frequency f: waves per second (Hz)
  • Amplitude: max displacement
  • Wavelength λ: compression to compression
  • T = 1/f
  • Pitch ∝ f
  • Loudness ∝ A²
Echo & Reverberation
  • Echo: distinct reflection, min 17.2 m, gap ≥ 0.1 s
  • Reverberation: multiple overlapping echoes
  • Concert halls: soft materials absorb
Speed of Sound
  • In air at 25°C ≈ 346 m/s
  • Solids > Liquids > Gases
  • Cannot travel in vacuum
  • Temp↑ → speed↑
  • Mach 1 = speed of sound
Ultrasound Applications
  • Medical USG/sonography
  • Lithotripsy: breaks kidney stones
  • SONAR: depth/submarine
  • Industrial: detect cracks
  • Echolocation: bats/dolphins
